title: Unit testing a design
idea: A unit test runs one class in isolation with chosen inputs and checks one behaviour, so a broken rule fails fast with a name that says which rule.
points: Each test follows Arrange, Act, Assert: set up, call once, check the result.
Pick boundary inputs: just before, on and just after every limit.
Inject time, randomness and I/O through the constructor, so tests can freeze them.
Teams write these with JUnit 5; a hard-to-test class usually signals a design problem.

hero.caption: Rule: free up to 2 days late; after that, 25 cents for every day late, capped at 500. Off-by-one bugs live on the highlighted row.

code.title: Tests catch a boundary bug
code.caption: Six boundary tests run against a fee rule with one wrong comparison. Exactly one test names the broken rule.

walk.text: A tiny `check` stands in for JUnit's assertions: count and report each result.
Each test pins one rule, and its name reads like a line of the spec.
The boundary case: the last grace day must still be free.
The bug: `<` instead of `<=`. Every non-boundary input still gives the right fee.
Charged and capped cases pass, so only boundary tests would ever expose this.
The summary line shows how many rules hold and how many broke.

code.title: Fixed rule, frozen clock
code.caption: The fixed rule passes. `ReturnDesk` takes a `Clock`, so the test controls what today means.

walk.text: `ReturnDesk` asks the injected `Clock` for today instead of the system clock.
Arrange: freeze the clock five days after the due date.
Act and Assert in one line: five days late is 125 cents, on any machine.
`checkThrows` asserts the exception type, like JUnit's `assertThrows`.
Failure paths are behaviours too: a null due date must be rejected.
The fix is `<=`, plus guard clauses that name the missing argument.

pitfalls: Calling `LocalDate.now()` inside a class makes tests pass today and fail next month.
One test asserting five things hides which rule broke; split it into five named tests.
Testing private methods couples tests to internals; test through the public contract instead.

options: PASS grace day free / PASS not negative

quiz.why: With `<`, two days late is charged 50 cents, so the boundary test fails. The fee is still positive, so the second check passes.

takeaway: Test one behaviour per case, at the boundaries, with time injected.
